Exposures from population counts

Source: R/data-exposure.R
mt_as_exposure.Rd

Approximates person-years at risk from population stocks and stores them as the exposure table:

Usage

mt_as_exposure(data, type)

Arguments

data

An mt_data object with a population table.

type

The kind of population counts, a required choice: "midyear" (mid-year estimates, used as exposures), "jan1" (1 January) or "dec31" (31 December); see Details.

Value

The mt_data object with an exposure table.

Details

  • "midyear": the mid-year population of a calendar year is used as the exposure of that year;

  • "jan1": the exposure of year t is the mean of the January 1 populations of years t and t + 1 in the same age interval. The last year has no successor and is dropped.

  • "dec31": populations on 31 December of year t (as published by the German Federal Statistical Office); the exposure of year t is the mean of the populations on 31 December of years t - 1 and t. The first year has no predecessor and is dropped.

These are the standard approximations of person-years from population counts (Preston, Heuveline and Guillot 2001): the population at the middle of the year, or the mean of the populations at its start and its end. The HMD uses more refined cohort-based formulas. The approximation used is recorded in the provenance column.

References

Preston SH, Heuveline P, Guillot M (2001). Demography: Measuring and Modeling Population Processes. Blackwell.

Examples

p <- data.frame(year = 2001:2003, age = 70, population = c(1000, 990, 985))
x <- mt_as_exposure(mt_add_population(mt_data(), p), type = "jan1")
mt_obs(x, "exposure")
#>    stratum  label age_lo age_hi period_lo period_hi value      provenance
#>      <int> <char>  <num>  <num>     <num>     <num> <num>          <char>
#> 1:       1    all     70     71      2001      2002 995.0 population_jan1
#> 2:       1    all     70     71      2002      2003 987.5 population_jan1
